html:
Warren Hastings was the first governor-general of British India, in office from 1773 to 1785. He turned the East India Company's loose hold on Bengal into a working government, and was then put on trial for how he had done it.

He came to India at seventeen and learnt Persian and Bengali. As governor of Bengal from 1772 he ended the pretence that the nawab still ruled: Company officers now collected the taxes and ran the courts, with Hindu and Muslim law applied to each community.

He admired Indian learning. He backed the founding of the Asiatic Society, paid for the first English translation of the Bhagavad Gita and opened a college for Muslim law in Calcutta.

His years were full of war, against the Marathas and against Hyder Ali of Mysore (see the Anglo-Mysore Wars), with little help from Britain, which was losing America. To pay for it he squeezed the Company's allies: he fined the raja of Varanasi and forced the royal ladies of Awadh to hand over their treasure.

Back in London he was impeached. Edmund Burke led the case before the House of Lords. The trial ran from 1788 to 1795 and ended in his acquittal. It set the idea that British power in India must answer to Parliament.
sum: Warren Hastings was the first governor-general of British India, in office from 1773 to 1785. He turned the East India Company's loose hold on Bengal into a working government, and was then put on trial for how he had done it.
